title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming formatting
author: Jordan Kim
description: Motivation: bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with OpenAI semantics for parameter handling (temperature/top_p/n), role-preserving chat inputs, stop sequence behavior, propagation of logprobs and token-level metadata, and stable streaming formatting for both regular responses and tool/function calls. This change fixes several behavioral mismatches surfaced by SDK users and downstream integrations: inconsistent handling of `roles` when caller-provided roles differ from internal canonicalization, stop-sequence edge cases that produced truncated final tokens, incorrect logprobs offsets when streaming, and non-deterministic chunk boundaries for function call streaming that broke client parsers. Changes: - API surface: update openai-compat handler to accept legacy param aliases and normalize params to Redwood runtime config. - Role handling: preserve original role ordering and names, add normalization for assistant/system/user when omitted. - Stop sequences: implement token-aware stop detection in runtime to avoid partial-token truncation; add unit/integration tests. - Logprobs: ensure per-token logprobs are emitted consistently in both streaming and non-streaming modes; add offset alignment fixes. - Streaming formatting: stabilize chunk envelope format for tool/function calls and structured outputs, and document the SSE framing for clients. - Backwards compatible: maintain legacy endpoint behavior when legacy_mode flag is set. Testing and rollout: comprehensive unit tests added, integration tests against the openai-compat e2e harness, and a staged rollout via feature flag. See files changed for details and a short migration note for SDKs and consumers.
commits: 3 commits: 1) Normalize openai params and role canonicalization (Jordan Kim) 2) Token-aware stop detection and logprob offset fixes (Jordan Kim) 3) Streaming envelope stabilization and tests (Jordan Kim)
review_comments: Alex: Requested explicit tests for stop sequences that split tokens across chunks and for multi-stop lists; asked to document the exact SSE framing for streaming function calls. Priya: Noted risk around performance on small batch sizes introduced by token-aware stop detection; asked for perf numbers and a threshold toggle. Diego: Suggested adding a compatibility flag to preserve old behavior during staged rollout. Responses: added tests for token-splitting stops and multi-stop lists; added a microbenchmark in runtime showing <1% median latency impact at default batch sizes, with a `legacy_mode` flag (openai-compat) to disable token-aware truncation if customers opt out. Updated docs with streaming SSE framing and example parsers. All reviewers approved after changes.
ci_checks: Checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (flaky - one job failed on first run but passed after rerun), lint (pass), e2e-streaming (pass). Notes: integration-tests job retried once due to known flakiness in test harness; rerun succeeded.
merge_summary: Squash-merged by Priya Patel. Message: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - normalize params, fix role/stop/logprob semantics, stabilize streaming formatting. Includes tests and docs. Rollout: feature-flag gated; enabled for 10% of traffic for 24h then ramped to 100% after monitoring window.
release_notes: Aligns /v1/chat.completions behavior with OpenAI semantics for params (temperature/top_p/n), preserves role order and names, fixes stop-sequence truncation at token boundaries, ensures consistent per-token logprobs in streaming and non-streaming modes, and stabilizes streaming envelope formatting for tool/function calls. Backwards-compatible via `legacy_mode` flag. SDKs updated with migration guidance.
notes: Migration: SDK maintainers should pick up the openai-compat client update. Consumers relying on previous partial-token truncation should enable `legacy_mode` temporarily. Monitoring: added alerts for increased 5xxs or stream parsing errors under openai-compat feature flag.
testing_summary: Added unit tests covering: param aliasing, role canonicalization, multi-stop sequences including token-splitting edge cases, logprob offset alignment. Added integration e2e tests for streaming function/tool call envelopes and an example client parser. Performance: microbenchmarks show median P50 latency increase <1% under representative workloads; CPU/GPU utilization unchanged in baseline tests.
security_review: security: no new secrets or KMS changes; surface changes limited to request normalization and streaming framing. Threat model: streaming envelope stabilization reduces client parsing mistakes; no new data exfiltration paths identified.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-2040: Add telemetry to track how many customers opt into legacy_mode. ENG-2041: Update SDK release notes and bump package versions. ENG-2042: Run a 48h canary in prod region eu-west-1 focusing on streaming-heavy customers.
customer_impact: Fixes several customer-reported incompatibilities with OpenAI behavior (stop/logprobs/roles). May require SDK updates; migration path documented.
example_request:
POST /v1/chat.completions with { model: "rw-openai-compat-1", messages: [{role:"user", content:"Hello"}], temperature:0.7, n:2, stop:["
"] } returns aligned responses with preserved roles and consistent logprobs
